universalAnswers.whatHappened: A September 14 peer-reviewed study reported simultaneous decoding of limited attempted speech and gesture outputs from a single implanted ECoG array in three participants with severe paralysis.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: A brain-computer interface turns recorded brain activity into commands for an external device.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: The cited peer-reviewed paper and NIH release were captured as complete normal-web source outputs.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: Three participants, limited trained expressions, wired external processing and further testing needs; no patient outcomes or availability claim.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: Readers can distinguish a communication-access research step from a treatment claim.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: People with severe paralysis and readers of health-AI reporting; no personal recommendation is established.
universalAnswers.changesNow: The study demonstrates a research interface, not a released device.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Larger cohorts and broader repertoires are still required.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Ask who used the system, what was decoded and whether it was tested in ordinary care.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Was this a prepared research task or a clinical result?

health-science.aiRole: Parallel decoders matched recorded ECoG signals to limited speech and gesture outputs.
health-science.professionalRole: Researchers still choose follow-up questions and conduct biological validation; the report describes laboratory tests of a nearby stretch of DNA after a ranked research case.
health-science.evidenceLevel: An 83-page technical research report with benchmarks, one rare-disease case and one laboratory experiment, not an approval or routine clinical service.
health-science.benefitClaim: The report measures prioritization and interpretation of variants; it does not measure improved diagnosis, treatment, or patient outcomes.
health-science.risksAndFalseResults: A prediction may be wrong or irrelevant in a particular cell type or person, so treating it as a diagnosis could create false certainty; this is a boundary rather than a measured patient harm.
health-science.availability: Wired research setup only; no patient-ready pathway verified.
health-science.readerBoundary: This research explanation is not medical advice and is not a reason to interpret a personal genetic result or change care.

research-benchmark.researchQuestion: Can one implanted array support parallel speech-and-gesture decoding?
research-benchmark.method: Three participants; limited trained tasks and concurrent decoding.
research-benchmark.result: Proof-of-concept avatar output, not treatment outcome.
research-benchmark.sponsorAndInterests: Google DeepMind researchers and academic collaborators authored the report; the primary report is the basis for research claims.
research-benchmark.independentReplication: No independent replication has been verified for this candidate; Nature coverage is independent reporting, not a replication study.
research-benchmark.realWorldTransfer: Precomputed scores can speed a research search, but a useful variant still needs validation in the relevant biological setting before any clinical conclusion.
research-benchmark.limitations: Small cohort and restricted repertoire; further testing needed.

translation.newsVersionExact: Researchers tested a thin sensor array placed on the brain’s motor cortex.
translation.actualMeaningExact: This peer-reviewed proof of concept is not an available treatment or proof of better health outcomes.
translation.mechanismExact: Two decoders matched those patterns to a limited set of phrases and gestures.
translation.familiarExampleExact: For the next health-AI headline, ask who used the system, what it did, and whether it was tested in ordinary care.
